[i]"My Princess asked for room service?"[/i] she chuckled, bringing the cart to the bedside. It had several covered plates, with grilled ham-steaks, eggs, and other breakfast items. In addition, there were two mugs, a small pitcher of cream, sugar, and a small pot with coffee. She sat back on the bed and kissed her partner on the cheek.[/quote]

Cecilia had slipped on the black turtleneck she had arrived with by the time Elena returned. She sat up against the backboard of the bed and fixed up her messy hair. Her lips formed a smile in excitement.

[i]Lets eat![/i] She brought the food closer to herself, serving a plate full of food and passing it to Elena before grabbing one for herself.

[quote=corzerran;61254294]Cecilia had slipped on the black turtleneck she had arrived with by the time Elena returned. She sat up against the backboard of the bed and fixed up her messy hair. Her lips formed a smile in excitement.

[i]Lets eat![/i] She brought the food closer to herself, serving a plate full of food and passing it to Elena before grabbing one for herself.[/quote]
Elena started eating contentedly, enjoying the quiet moment. The sun cast a golden glow on the room, and the two chattered through their breakfast. They got ready for the day's plans: a trip out to the Iora Peninsula, a walk along the rocky shore. Elena took the afternoon to finish up a little work.
The rest of the couple's vacation in Koranvistan passed in relative peace, with a lot of sightseeing and a few places from Elena's past.
And soon, Elena was seeing her partner off at the airport, wishing for a way out of the time she'd have to wait.
She left Cecilia with a little note- a sketched ring and a "soon, sweetheart <3"

[Spoiler=tunnel warfare]
[I]with what little success F-14AN's had against the growlers now dissappeared. It is decided by air command to hand the defensive over to the much more advanced 4,5th gen uiterwaard trapdoor jets. These jets are integrated with multi-spectrum that disregards data corrupted by the growlers and is more resilient then the F-14AN's radar. An order is send out to the underground SAM facilities hidden by the dense forests to replace the radars of newly produced SAM with passive radar modes that can track emissions without active pinging and thus reduce spoofing vulnerability. At the same time the remaining SAM batteries get connected to cellular signals and FM radio to form a basic passive radar around the country without emitting it's own signal and get targeted by SEAD or growlers. Production of SAM shifts more to mobile SAM connected to passive radars to shoot-and-scoot using passive/semi-passive radar techniques. 

With the return of physical wires decentralized high command noticed more strikes on communication lines and after a brief meeting of 30 minutes it is decided to repeal the copper line decision except for a few small areas in the southeast of the country. The exceptions are buried 2 meters underground and reinforced with armored conduits to resist FAMM strikes with a few engineer teams on standby and with anti-drone weapons if neccesary. With the re-introduction of wireless communication the question of the jamming arised and another order is send out to military radio producers: integrate radio's with FHSS or DSSS until the military researchers come up with a better way to counter the growler. Most radio producers follow the new order while some decide to diversify and make the radio's transmit on very low power or in bursts that only looks like noise to the growler's recievers. Some regional/local commanders decide on enforcing EMCON/emissions control to reduce detection risk. small local producers step up their decoy emitter production to trick the growlers into wasting it's limited jamming resources on decoys. 

The F-14AN's pick up the tracking alert of the HDF's anti air missiles and quickly deploy flares and other countermeasures to try and shake off the missiles. 
With 5th gen aircraft moving closer to the mainland the uiterwaard trapdoor jets face an dnormous challdnge of trying to shoot down the stealth aircraft. Some scientists come up with the idea of integrating link 16 for 'silent' ambushes, only ambush/attack 5th gen jets in squadrons if forced to engage and only use IRST for potential passive lock-ons without being detected, if the jets even can get close to the HDF's 5th gen planes. 

On the ground soldiers and paramilitary quickly work to fully decentralize stored army fuel and ammo into much smaller caches spread out over the country. Mobile AAA and short-range SAM gets dispersed around cities and other targets to try and create denial bubbles while civilians and army engineers try to quickly repair the damaged infrastructure and try to get it back up again in a short while. Other engineer units use inflatable decoys like parked MLRS battalions and SAM sites that looks realistic from high in the sky to try and bait the hochdeutsche into firing missiles at the decoys.[/i] 

[I]On sea the warships of the navy form a semi-circle around their homeports to strengthen anti-air defense a bit against the Hochdeutsche missiles while several sailors and a few marines deploy anti-torpedo nets they fetched from the port. Even if the ships would get sunk the wreckages then would block the port and prevent any ship from trying to access it.[/i] 

[B]landing and aftermath[/b]
[I]alarms ring throughout the bunkers and coastal turrets after the HDF strikes and the incoming assault. Machine guns get loaded, killzones get prepared and the remaining undamaged or lightly damaged Anti ship missile batteries and turret batteries turn to the sea and prepare to sink any troop transports that try to land while several coastal batteries of battleship caliber that are 5 to 8 kilometers in the back starts to turn on and rotate to the beach ready to provide artillery fire. Soon another problem arised, hochdeutsche helicopters that suppressed the machine gun fire and drones that detonated the mines. Luckily for the defenders there is a batch of flyswatter MANPADS nearby to deal with the helicopters and a very few cruise missiles who fly a bit too slow and close enough for the flyswatter to get a lock on. Plus several ruisgen 4X4 trucks in the back that are modified with twin 30mm cannons that can engage helicopters and drones. But for the soldiers who can't get a MANPADS they used shotguns loaded with birdshot or buckshot instead. 
When the enemy armor starts to land the defenders start using MAT-9 arrow ATGM's and RW2015 rocket launchers against the enemy armor. In the sky a flight of 4 Fokker G.VD CAS take of from a small rudimentary airfield armed with guided bombs and AGM's, once they are i  distance of firing their bonbs and missiles they quickly do a strafing run of hochdeutsche landing boats using AGM's and leave again to a different rudimentary airfield deep in the country. 
(At this point i dunno how to describe the beach scene further.[/i]
[B]insert saving private ryan beach scene but with modern equipment and a lot more shell holes[/b]) 

[I]Despite the resistance the defending soldiers put up, the marineinfanterie eventually broke through because of their numerical superiority and constant bombardments. the soldiers in the forts quickly evacuated but not before setting up hidden traps in the forts and surrounding buildings[/i] 

[B]description about the area surrounding the beach: mostly dense forests with a few small (coastal) towns scattered around. Ideal for vietnam-style tunnels and traps[/b]
[I]in the area some militia and reserve units, totalling 3500 soldiers have heard the noises from the beach and quickly started digging hidden trenches 3,4 meters deep, mining certain roads with several fox holes hidden in the dense vegetation alongside the road incase a MRAP runs over a mine. Throughout the day small reinforcements, mostly dispersed, travel to the beachhead to prepare ambushes and help the others dig tunnels and conceal the entrance points to blend in with the enviroment and with rooms deep enough where cruise missiles can't reach. Once night falls the majority of the reinforcements, 30000 total with several saturation MLRS and artillery and multispectral thermal nets for the ambush points, travel to the beachhead. Once there the MLRS start to bombard the beachhead and quickly leave under the cover of the night while dozens of drones gets launched that target vehicles, beached ships and supplies on land. At the same time small skirmish attacks comprised of mostly AFV's, jeeps and a few MBT's would attack the flanks and leave before reinforcements could come to the marineinfanterie's aid 

At the diplomatic front several low ranking diplomats request the NR foreign ministry to start the first round of peace talks in orphogron.[/i][/spoiler]
